excerpts.text: Martinis were awarded the prize "for the discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantization in an electric circuit" according to the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

In the mid-80s, Clarke, Devoret, and Martinis conducted a [series of experiments](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2025/popular-information/) on macroscopic quantum tunneling and energy quantization. They created circuits using superconductors separated by thin insulating barriers known as Josephson junctions. These allow for currents with no electrical resistance, and under the right conditions, collective quantum states can be formed. They demonstrated that such a circuit could remain in a “zero-voltage” state but still, via quantum tunneling, escape that state in a way that is forbidden by classical physics.
